text_en: Actions are but by intentions, and every man shall have only that which he intended.

Islam has been built on five pillars: testifying that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, paying zakat, making pilgrimage to the House, and fasting in Ramadan.
None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.

Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him be generous to his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.
The strong is not the one who overcomes others by his strength, but the strong is the one who controls himself when angry.
Religion is sincerity. We said: To whom? He said: To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and to the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk.
Whoever calls others to guidance will have a reward equal to the rewards of those who follow him, without diminishing their reward in the slightest.
A man said to the Prophet, peace be upon him: Advise me. He said: Do not become angry. The man asked repeatedly, and each time he said: Do not become angry.
Cleanliness is half of faith. Saying 'alhamdulillah' fills the scale. 'Subhan Allah' and 'alhamdulillah' fill what is between the heavens and the earth.
The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

No one with even an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise. A man said: But a man loves that his clothes and shoes be beautiful. He said: Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting truth and looking down on people.
Allah does not look at your bodies or your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter.
Make things easy and do not make them difficult. Give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.
The most beloved of you to me, and the nearest in seating to me on the Day of Resurrection, are those of you with the best character.
A good word is charity.
Whoever guides someone to good will have a reward equal to that of the one who does it.

Every Muslim must give charity. They asked: What if he has nothing? He said: Let him work with his hands, benefit himself, and give in charity. They asked: What if he cannot? He said: Let him help one who is in need and oppressed. They asked: What if he cannot? He said: Let him enjoin good. They asked: What if he cannot? He said: Let him refrain from evil — that is charity for him.
The world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever.
The most beloved of deeds to Allah are those done consistently, even if they are few.
Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.

I asked the Prophet, peace be upon him: Which deed is most beloved to Allah? He said: Prayer at its proper time. I asked: Then what? He said: Kindness to parents. I asked: Then what? He said: Jihad in the way of Allah.
The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin with those who are your dependents. The best charity is that which is given when one is wealthy and self-sufficient.
Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of all good.
When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: a continuing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.
Smiling at your brother is charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity. Guiding a man in the land of the lost is charity. Removing a harmful thing from the path is charity.

Whoever relieves a believer's distress in this world, Allah will relieve his distress on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things easy for one in difficulty, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the next. Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah will cover him in this world and the next. Allah helps His servant as long as the servant helps his brother.

There are three things that whoever has them will find the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are more beloved to him than anything else, that he loves a person only for the sake of Allah, and that he hates to return to disbelief as he hates to be thrown into the fire.
Two words light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih, Subhan Allahil 'Adheem.

Whoever says 'La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadeer' a hundred times in a day will have the reward of freeing ten slaves, a hundred good deeds will be written for him, a hundred sins will be erased from him, and he will be protected from Satan that day until evening.
